title.en: Calm mind, flexible body, balanced breath

text.en: Exam pressure and daily expectations can trigger stress, racing heartbeat, and tension. Yoga offers practical postures, breathing, cleansing kriyas, and relaxation to restore balance.

Adolescents face stress from high expectations, causing physiological (heart rate, blood pressure) and psychological (attention, emotion) changes. Since stress cannot be avoided, it must be managed.
Yoga as a way of life includes Mitahara (wholesome food in a calm mind), Achara (right conduct), and positive Vichara (thoughts).
Standing, sitting, prone, and supine asanas—such as Hastottanasana, Padahastasana, Trikonasana, Shashankasana, Ushtrasana, Ardhamatsyendrasana, Bhujangasana, Makarasana, Sarvangasana, Matsyasana, and Shavasana—tone muscles, improve spine flexibility, and calm nerves.
Kapalabhati is a cleansing kriya (not a pranayama) that revitalises the nervous system, though people with high blood pressure, hernia, or vertigo should avoid it.
Pranayama regulates breath: Anuloma-Viloma (alternate nostril breathing), Bhastrika (quick deep breaths), Bhramari (humming bee sound), and Sheetali (cooling breath).
Yoganidra ('sleep with awareness' in Shavasana) and Meditation release deep bodily tension and bring mental peace.
We cannot eliminate all stress, so managing stress through yoga is essential.
Mitahara means eating the right quality and quantity of food in a calm, positive state of mind.
Asanas like Trikonasana, Bhujangasana, and Shavasana stretch the spine and relax body and mind.
Kapalabhati is a cleansing kriya; always follow safety limitations for blood pressure or back pain.
Pranayamas like Anuloma-Viloma and Bhramari (humming bee) calm the nervous system.
Yoganidra is 'sleep with awareness' practised in Shavasana to dissolve tension.

problem.en: A student feels anxious before an exam and wants a safe, calming breathing practice. Which pranayama is ideal, and which kriya should someone with high BP avoid?

text.en: Practise Anuloma-Viloma (alternate nostril breathing) or Bhramari (humming bee).

why.en: Both calm the mind and balance the nervous system.

text.en: Someone with high BP or cardiac issues should avoid Kapalabhati and Bhastrika.

why.en: Chapter 8 lists high BP and cardiac problems as limitations for rapid forceful breathing.

prompt.en: Explain what Yoganidra is and name two pranayamas with their benefits.

requiredIdeas.en: Yoganidra is sleep with awareness practised in Shavasana for deep relaxation
Anuloma-Viloma (alternate nostril) calms mind and nourishes with oxygen
Bhramari (humming bee) reduces stress; Sheetali cools body and mind

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking Kapalabhati is safe for everyone regardless of high BP or hernia

points.en: Yoga manages stress via lifestyle (Mitahara, Achara), asanas, kriyas, pranayama, Yoganidra, and meditation.
Every asana and pranayama has specific benefits and safety limitations.
Pranayamas include Anuloma-Viloma, Bhastrika, Bhramari, and Sheetali.
Yoganidra ('sleep with awareness') and meditation deeply relax body and mind.
